verification_policy: Include only project identities, descriptions, publications, findings, and media supported by inspected official NASA sources. NTRS document identifiers are not NASA investigation identifiers.

experiments.title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments (ACME)
experiments.summary: NASA describes ACME as fundamental microgravity combustion research intended to improve efficiency and reduce pollutant emissions in practical terrestrial combustion.
experiments.description: NTRS describes six independent ACME investigations of laminar, non-premixed gaseous-fuel flames conducted on the ISS in the Combustion Integrated Rack from November 2017 to February 2022.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: ACME conducts fundamental microgravity combustion research to improve efficiency and reduce pollutant emissions in practical terrestrial combustion.

sections.title: Investigations and research setting
sections.content: NASA's 2022 ACME poster describes six independent investigations of laminar, non-premixed gaseous-fuel flames conducted on the ISS in the Combustion Integrated Rack from November 2017 to February 2022.

experiments.title: Burning and Suppression of Solids (BASS)
experiments.summary: NASA describes BASS as an investigation of the burning and extinction characteristics of varied solid-fuel samples in microgravity.
experiments.description: The inspected NASA results include BASS-II documentation. The BASS-II summary report describes tests that varied oxygen concentration, ventilation flow, and fuel type, thickness, and geometry.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: BASS examines the burning and extinction characteristics of a wide variety of fuel samples in microgravity.

sections.title: BASS-II results scope
sections.content: The BASS-II summary report describes the test variables and reports combustion-gas readings and calculated heat-release results. This catalog does not reproduce or reinterpret its numerical measurements.

experiments.review_notes: DAFT is described as a precursor/risk-mitigation activity supporting SAME, not as the SAME investigation itself.
experiments.title: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test (DAFT)
experiments.summary: NASA describes DAFT as a feasibility test of a modified P-Trak instrument intended to support the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment (SAME) in microgravity.
experiments.description: A NASA NTRS article describes DAFT as risk mitigation developed at NASA Glenn with ZIN Technologies to evaluate a condensation nuclei counter during long-duration microgravity operation. A later NASA presentation reports the precursor flight's cabin particle measurement context.

sections.title: Instrument feasibility
sections.content: DAFT evaluated whether a modified P-Trak condensation nuclei counter could operate properly in long-duration microgravity as a key SAME diagnostic.

sections.title: Precursor measurement context
sections.content: A NASA presentation reports that DAFT flew as a precursor and provided an ISS cabin background-particle measurement. Its abstract characterizes the measured background as below the cited spacecraft maximum allowable concentration; this is reported here only as the presentation's statement.

experiments.title: Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX)
experiments.summary: NASA says FLEX was designed to assess inert-gas suppressant effectiveness in microgravity and estimate the limiting oxygen index for steady combustion.
experiments.description: NASA's NTRS record provides a technical publication titled Detailed Results from the Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX), covering the March 2009 to December 2011 test period. The source describes results and does not provide an experiment-specific NASA identifier.

sections.title: Objectives
sections.content: Assess and quantify inert-gas suppressant effectiveness in microgravity and obtain a conservative estimate of the limiting oxygen index for steady combustion.

sections.title: Results publication
sections.content: NASA NTRS provides a detailed FLEX results publication covering tests from March 2009 through December 2011. No measurement values are copied into this catalog.

experiments.title: Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration (Saffire)
experiments.mission: Cygnus cargo spacecraft after departure from the ISS
experiments.summary: NASA's Saffire series investigated spacecraft fire safety. NASA NTRS describes the series as spacecraft fire experiments conducted using a cargo vehicle after it departed the ISS.
experiments.description: The NASA archive entry names the project Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration. NASA NTRS documents the development and operation of Saffire installments, and NASA media metadata documents a Saffire-V materials test.

sections.title: Series scope
sections.content: NASA documents a series of spacecraft fire experiments; the cited publications and media identify individual Saffire installments rather than a single undifferentiated test.

sections.title: Saffire-V material test
sections.content: NASA's Saffire-V video metadata reports that fires in microgravity grew and burned faster on thinner ribs than on thicker sample regions in the described test. This observation is specific to the media-described test, not a universal quantitative result.

experiments.review_notes: SAME and SAME-2 are related but distinct run/record scopes. The NASA news article and NTRS record give differing year descriptions for the repeat; verify timeline and grouping before importing.
experiments.title: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment (SAME)
experiments.summary: NASA describes SAME as an investigation of smoke-particle characteristics relevant to distinguishing smoke from nuisance aerosols and improving spacecraft smoke detection.
experiments.description: NASA documentation describes experiments with smoke from spacecraft materials and particle-size measurements. A NASA NTRS publication specifically reports particle morphology and size results from SAME-2, which should not be silently treated as results from the initial run.

sections.title: Smoke characterization
sections.content: NASA describes the need to distinguish different smoke and aerosol types, including soot and recondensed polymer droplets, for spacecraft smoke detection.

sections.title: SAME-2 particle results
sections.content: NASA NTRS provides particle morphology and size results specifically from SAME-2. Keep those results scoped to the SAME-2 reflight; do not merge them into the initial SAME run without a verified relationship rule.

experiments.title: Structure & Liftoff in Combustion Experiment (SLICE)
experiments.summary: NASA describes SLICE as a study of coflow laminar diffusion flames, a configuration useful for experiments and numerical modeling.
experiments.description: NASA sources describe SLICE's ISS combustion research and NTRS provides experimental and computational publications on soot formation in coflow jet flames under microgravity and normal gravity.

sections.title: Research configuration
sections.content: Coflow laminar diffusion flames are used for combustion studies because the configuration supports accurate numerical modeling.

sections.title: Soot-formation research
sections.content: NASA NTRS documents an experimental and computational study of soot formation in a coflow jet flame under microgravity and normal gravity. No numerical measurements are copied into this catalog.

experiments.title: Smoke Point in Co-flow Experiment (SPICE)
experiments.summary: NASA describes SPICE as a continuation of fundamental work on the stability and extinction of jet diffusion flames, with a focus on smoke-point behavior.
experiments.description: The inspected NTRS record describes planned coflowing-oxidizer flame measurements to study smoke-point properties and validate flame models. It is written prospectively and does not establish that the experiment was completed or report completed findings.

sections.title: Planned objectives
sections.content: The NTRS record describes planned measurements of non-buoyant jet diffusion flame smoke-point properties across fuels and nozzle/coflow configurations, as well as flame-shape, stabilization-height, and temperature measurements.
